newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary scandal weakens faith in political system.
newsitem.headline: Hungary scandal weakens faith in political system.

text.p: Hungary's privatisation scandal has undermined confidence in the government and in politicians, a public opinion poll showed on Monday.

The poll was made in early October when former minister of industry and trade Tamas Suchman and the state privatisation agency APV's board of directors were sacked in a scandal over irregular payments to a consultant, Marta Tocsik.
The sackings followed press reports in September about irregular payments of millions of dollars from APV to Tocsik.

Socialist Prime Minister Gyula Horn's popularity fell by five percentage points to 38 points in the poll. Almost all politicians covered by the survey, including most opposition leaders, dropped by one to five percentage points.

"Confidence in the government and mainly in the larger party of the coalition (the Socialists) has weakened significantly," said the Marketing Centrum Institution poll published in the daily Nepszava newspaper.
"The loss of confidence has affected the whole system of political institutions and almost all politicians," it added.
